analysis.title: Earnings Blast (Raymond James Investment Strategy), November 2, 2026
key_insights: Last week's results from the largest US hyperscalers were mixed. AI-driven cloud demand was overshadowed by softer than expected capex commentary.
Because hyperscaler capex came in slightly softer than expected, markets will focus on AMD's results on Tuesday evening (11/3) for more insight into AI infrastructure spending.
The S&P 500 sector table shows EPS growth of 29.6%, a beat rate of 80.9% and sales growth of 12.8%. The report headlines this as the third consecutive quarter of 25%+ EPS growth.

Information Technology leads the large sectors with EPS growth of 65.1%, a 92.9% beat rate and sales growth of 40.1%. Energy shows the highest EPS growth at 146.3%, with a 100.0% beat rate and sales growth of 26.7%.
Consumer Discretionary has the weakest EPS growth at 0.7% and a 66.7% beat rate. Health Care (4.5%) and Consumer Staples (3.1%) are also at the low end, while Consumer Staples has a 100.0% beat rate.
About 21% of S&P 500 market cap reports during the week of 11/2 to 11/6. Information Technology is the largest sector share at 11%.

Microsoft guided Azure revenue growth to 49% to 50% in constant currency. It said some third-party GPU-as-a-Service contracts were delayed to H2 and customer demand continues to exceed available supply.
Alphabet said Google Cloud revenues grew 103% and that year-over-year query growth is the highest in five years. It is working to bring more capacity online.
Amazon said AWS grew 39.3% year-over-year, accelerating for the sixth straight quarter and the fastest growth in nearly five years. AWS backlog is $578 billion.
The report's S&P 500 forward estimate chart shows 3Q26 consensus EPS estimates rising from Nov-25 to Sep-26, which the report titles 'Forward Estimates March Higher'.

Energy 3Q26 reported results: EPS growth 146.3%, beat rate 100.0%, sales growth 26.7%.
Microsoft guidance given on its call: Azure revenue growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency (company guidance, not yet reported).
Alphabet reported Google Cloud revenue growth of 103%. Amazon reported AWS growth of 39.3% year-over-year with a $578 billion backlog.
AMD reports Tuesday evening 11/3. The report treats it as the next read on AI infrastructure spending after softer than expected hyperscaler capex.
risk_factors: Softer than expected capex commentary from US hyperscalers could weigh on AI infrastructure spending expectations.
Delayed third-party GPU-as-a-Service contracts at Microsoft pushed some revenue to H2.
Microsoft cited a strong prior-year comparison, including accelerating growth in the second half, as a factor in future year-over-year growth.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-driven cloud demand is strong. Google Cloud grew 103%, AWS grew 39.3% with a $578 billion backlog, and Microsoft says customer demand continues to exceed available supply.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex commentary from the largest US hyperscalers was slightly softer than expected, which overshadowed the cloud demand results.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AMD's earnings results on Tuesday evening (11/3), which the report names as the next read on AI infrastructure spending.
